concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor conceded there is no admissible evidence that required pre-launch disclosure has already been completed. This concern was not closed.
The Actor conceded the exposed enterprise refund workflow segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort and that rollout controls do not exclude it.
The Actor conceded the risk acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved, and does not address the exposed segment. No approved exception was supplied.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence. The response narrows the certification theory and correctly concedes that rollout controls, rollback capability, and aggregate readiness do not satisfy the disclosure-policy predicate while the affected use case remains exposed. That reframing is useful but it is still a reinterpretation of the same record, not evidence that disclosure was completed, the use case was excluded, or approved risk acceptance exists. Aggregate readiness and reversible rollout support a bounded operational-readiness case, but they do not cure the unresolved model-card disclosure requirement. On this record, full compliance and compliant_with_caveats are not supported because the caveat is itself the unresolved compliance predicate.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch disclosure was completed for the exposed enterprise refund workflow use case.
The affected enterprise refund workflow segment remains eligible in the initial 4% rollout cohort.
No approved risk acceptance covers the exposed enterprise refund workflow exposure.
The certification theory still depends on caveated future documentation rather than a completed policy-satisfying artifact in the record.
